stories.notes: Spec run already completed (runId 20260730T142824Z) with both openspec and speckit assigned and applied. Coordinator review verdict is 'needs_review' with quality score 0.55 — key issues: openspec did not produce ACs, speckit authored baseline ACs instead of reviewing, no story splits generated despite multi-platform complexity, and no source files were reviewed by either agent. These gaps require human intervention (validate ACs against actual codebase, determine story splits, confirm SDK integration approach) rather than another automated spec cycle. Re-running the same agents without source file access would likely reproduce the same shortcomings. No further automated spec work warranted at this time.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline breakdown confirmed. Only openspec ran (assignedAgents and appliedAgents both list ['openspec'] only); speckit was never executed despite coordinatorNotes referencing speckit's work. Acceptance criteria remain empty ([]) — openspec's contribution notes claim 'ACs authored by openspec' but acceptanceChanged is false and no ACs exist in the story. No story splits were generated (splitChildren: []) despite the multi-platform complexity (GO, UP, MX) flagged in coordinator notes. The existing coordinatorReview references speckit authoring 12 ACs, but no speckit agentContributions entry exists and ACs are empty — this metadata is contradictory and likely describes a prior or phantom run. Both agents did NOT add meaningful, non-overlapping value because only one agent ran and it failed to produce its primary deliverable. Human review is required to: (1) author baseline acceptance criteria validated against actual source files (src/services/contentstack.ts, src/hooks/useContent.ts), (2) determine story splits by platform or concern, (3) re-run the full pipeline (openspec then speckit) once ACs exist.
